head_commit.message:
feat(start-sdk): add setupPrimaryUrl (#4030)

* feat(start-sdk): add setupPrimaryUrl and the configured address view

The "Set Primary URL" watcher every package hand-rolls raises a critical
task whenever the stored URL is missing from the interface's reachable
addresses. That list loses `.local` while the address table is rebuilt
and whenever the LAN IP is down, so a server that initializes services
without its LAN address, or loses the link, stops the service and asks the
user to pick the URL they already had.

`sdk.setupPrimaryUrl()` owns the pattern: the action, the init hook and a
reactive reader over the package's own store field. The hook judges the
choice against the interface's configured addresses, follows the hostname
through a port or scheme change, and clears the task once the hostname is
back. A `.local` choice is judged only while some LAN interface is up, the
always-on container bridge not counting. An IP choice is judged only while
the interface it came from is up; the hook records that interface when the
URL is stored, in a file beside the store named after it and the action
id, so no caller model or second helper instance can claim it, and a
damaged record reads as none. An IP whose interface it never saw is left
alone, since another interface's address is no evidence about it. A
domain or Tor choice is judged at once, as those rows never come and go
with the link.

A choice judged gone is replaced by `defaultUrl`'s pick, the `.local`
address unless the package says otherwise, which is what the services
that already handle this do. A package whose users must be told rather
than moved passes `onRemoved: 'task'`, raised at `important` unless told
otherwise; the task is also raised when nothing is left to fall back to.

`addressInfo.configured` exposes the unpruned enabled rows for it, and for
any package that needs "one of my addresses" rather than "reachable now".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* feat(start-sdk): take the primary URL through get/set and resolve it on read

`sdk.setupPrimaryUrl()` now takes `get`/`set` functions over the package's
own storage in place of a `FileHelper` and field projections, and the
action metadata in the shape `sdk.Action.withInput` takes. It returns the
action, `effective(effects)` and `createTask(effects, severity, options)`.

`effective` is the stored URL at its hostname's current port and scheme,
else the `.local` address, else the first. It is resolved on each read and
re-runs its caller when the choice or the addresses change, so the store
keeps the user's choice and a returning address is used again. That
retires the init hook's overwrite, the sidecar recording which interface
an IP came from, and the per-kind link-state checks.

`createTask` declares the interface's addresses as an `input-not-matches`
task's accepted input, so StartOS activates the task while the stored URL
is unset or gone and clears it when the user picks one or the address
returns. Severity is required, as for `createOwnTask`.

`onRemoved`, `severity`, `defaultUrl`, `read` and the English defaults are
gone. `addressInfo.configured` is dropped too: since #4035 a filled
address keeps `.local` while no LAN IP is up, so `nonLocal` is the view.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* refactor(start-sdk): rename primaryUrl.effective to bestUsable

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* refactor(start-sdk): return bestUsable as a reader and the task as an init script

bestUsable(effects) subscribed its caller with an implicit .const(), and
createTask(effects, …) did the same to the init hook calling it. bestUsable
now returns a Watchable, so the caller picks const/once/watch/onChange/
waitFor; it runs the package's get under a child effects whose constRetry
feeds its own change stream, as setupInit does for its handlers, and wakes
its caller only when the resolved URL changes. The task becomes
setupTask(severity, options), an InitScript registered with setupInit
whose re-run on an address change is its own.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* fix(start-sdk): build bestUsable from its sources' watch streams

bestUsable ran the package's get under effects.child() with a fixed name,
and CallbackHolder.child() ends the context of the same-named child it
replaces, so a second read on the same effects silently ended the first
read's subscription. get is now a reader in the shape FileHelper.read()
returns, and BestUsable merges its watch() stream with the host's under
the Watchable's own abort signal, with no child effects.

The tests' effects double now follows CallbackHolder's child and
leave-context rules, and cover a .const() surviving later reads on the
same effects.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* refactor(start-core,start-sdk): add Watchable.combine and build bestUsable on it

Combining readers is a general composition, so it lives on Watchable:
Watchable.combine(effects, sources, fn) is a reader over several
sources that re-evaluates fn when any of them changes, with every
source's watch tied to the combined reader's abort signal. bestUsable
drops its hand-rolled stream merge for it.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* refactor(start-core): declare Watchable implements WatchSource

Export WatchSource alongside Watchable.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* refactor(start-core): take map and eq in Watchable.combine

combine's raw value is the tuple of its sources' values, and it takes the
same optional map and eq as every other reader, emitting when map's result
differs from the last by eq.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* refactor(start-core): type readers by the WatchSource interface

Watchable's protected mapFn carries Raw into its structural type, so a
Watchable<A, X> is not a Watchable<B, X>. WatchSource is now the whole
reader interface (const, once, watch, onChange, waitFor) that Watchable
implements; combine and bestUsable return it, so consumers see only the
value they read.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5

* refactor(start-core)!: split MappedWatchable out of Watchable

Watchable<A> is typed only by the value it reads; its protected mapFn had
carried the raw type into every reader's structural type. A reader that
maps a raw value extends MappedWatchable<Raw, Mapped> and implements
fetchRaw/produceRaw, which GetHostInfo, GetServiceManifest, FileHelper's
reader and combine now do. Both fetch loops share Watchable.poll.

WatchSource is back to once() and watch(abort), what combine needs, and
Watchable.from(effects, source, eq?) builds a reader from one.

Helix-Harness: claude-code
Helix-Model: claude-opus-5-5
